stem: I'll accept any job ___ I don't have to get up early.
explanation: 词义辨析。even if：即使，虽然；as long as：只要；in case：万一，假使；even though：即使。根据句意“只要不必早起，我会接受任何工作”可知，选 B。

stem: ___ of the two authors thinks that the danger of a nuclear war is increasing.
explanation: 词义辨析。none 表示三者及以上中没有一个；either 表示两者之中任一，谓语用单数；both 表示两者都，谓语用复数；neither 表示两者都不，谓语用单数。由谓语 thinks 可知排除 C，又因是两位作家排除 A，故选 D。

stem: I walked too much yesterday and ___ are still aching now.
explanation: 固定用法。表示身体部位的名词可以直接放在名词之前作定语。故选 B（my leg muscles）。

stem: In some countries, ___ is called “equality” does not really mean equal rights for all people.
explanation: 主语从句。分析句子结构可知本句含主语从句，空处引导主语从句并在从句中作主语，符合条件的只有 what，故选 C。

stem: ___ we have finished the course, we shall start revision and prepare for the final exams.
explanation: 词义辨析。by now：到目前为止；now that：既然，引导原因状语从句；for now：目前，暂时；ever since：从那时起。根据句意可知，选 B。

stem: The bridge was named ___ the hero who had given his life to save a child.
explanation: 词语搭配。name…after…是固定搭配，意为“以……而命名”。故选 A。

stem: There is no ___ in insisting on the impossible.
explanation: 词语搭配。There is no sense in doing sth. 为常用句型，表示“做某事没有意义”。故选 D。

stem: The Internet of the fourth generation is now in the experimental stage. The time will come when it ___ possible for ordinary people to use it in their daily life.
explanation: 动词时态。第二句含有由 when 引导的定语从句，主句为一般将来时，从句用一般现在时表将来。故选 A。

stem: The shopping mall built a few months ago is ___ in the south of the city.
explanation: 词语搭配。be located in 为固定搭配，意为“位于”。lie 当“位于”讲时为不及物动词，无被动语态；laid 是 lay 的过去分词，意为“放置，安排”；place：放置。故选 A。

stem: It may be five to ten years ___ we can test this medicine on human patients.
explanation: 词义辨析。since：自从；after：在……之后；before：在……之前；when：当……的时候。根据句意“可能在 5 到 10 年之后我们才能测试这种药”可知，选 C。

stem: Bob, Dick and Tom ate 6, 8, and 10 years old ___.
explanation: 词义辨析。respectively：分别，各自；respectably：体面地，可敬地；没有 respectedly 一词；respectfully：恭敬地，有礼貌地。根据句意“分别为 6 岁、8 岁和 10 岁”可知，选 A。

stem: Children who are over-protected by their parents may become ___.
explanation: 词义辨析。hurt：受伤，损害；spoil：溺爱，宠坏；damage：损坏；harm：伤害，损害。根据句意“被父母过度保护的孩子可能会被宠坏”可知，选 B。

stem: Your explanation is still not easy enough to understand. Could you give any ___ examples?
explanation: 词义辨析。specific：明确的，详细的；special：特别的，专门的；specialist：专业的，专家的；spare：多余的，备用的。根据句意“给一些详细的例子”可知，选 A。

stem: Her ___ duties include cleaning the desks and mopping the floor. But she also needs to do many other things.
explanation: 词义辨析。continuous：连续不断的；routine：日常的，例行的；initial：最初的；constant：不变的，经常的。根据句意“日常工作”可知，选 B。

stem: Robert Owen's ideas were far ___ the age in which he lived.
explanation: 词义辨析。in front of：在……的前方，表示方位；advance in：在……改进、进步，B、C 两项是其分词形式；in advance of：超过，在……前面。根据句意“想法远超前于他所生活的时代”可知，选 D。

stem: Rural communities are usually more ___ in their child-rearing methods, while in the town there is more variety.
explanation: 词义辨析。uniform：一致的，相同的；like：类似的，通常作定语；similar：相似的，通常作表语；same：相同的，常作定语，前面加定冠词 the。根据句意及空处作表语可知，选 C。

stem: John Smith Community College is an educational institution ___ to providing higher education for all residents in the community.
explanation: 词义辨析。be committed to 意为“致力于”，其中 to 为介词，后接名词或动名词；contribute to 意为“向……贡献、捐赠”；combine 常与 with 搭配；assign sb. to 意为“指派某人到……”。根据句意可知，选 B。

stem: Mark often attempts to escape ___ whenever he breaks traffic rules.
explanation: 非谓语动词。escape doing sth. 意为“逃避做某事”，是固定用法，所以排除 B、C。根据 often 一词和谓语动词的时态可知，这里表示习惯性的行为，应用现在分词的一般式。故选 D。

stem: The police were accused of failing to ___ the people about the threat of the terrorists.
explanation: 词义辨析。speak：说话，其后常跟某种语言；tell：告诉，告知，其后可跟人；talk：谈话，不及物动词，不可直接跟宾语；say：说，其后一般跟说的内容。根据句意可知，选 B。

stem: Radio, television and press are ___ of conveying news and information.
explanation: 限定词词序。common 的最高级形式为 the most common；几个限定词同时修饰一个名词时，顺序大致为冠词、序数词、基数词、描绘性形容词等。故 three 应放在 most common 前，the 应放在 three 前，故选 B。

stem: Backward technologically ___ we are for the moment, we have perfect faith in our ability to catch up with the developed countries in time.
explanation: 状语从句。句前后为让步关系，应用 as 引导让步状语从句，as 引导的让步状语从句可以把表语或状语等提至句首，意为“尽管……”。if 引导条件状语从句；so 表因果；that 不可引导状语从句。故选 A。

stem: We don't need air conditioning, ___.
options: and neither can we afford it
and nor we can afford it
explanation: 倒装句。表示和前面情况相同时，否定句用 neither/nor 引起部分倒装结构；且 so、neither 和 nor 为连词，不需再用连词连接前后两个句子，可排除 A 项。故选 B。

stem: The Internet allows businessmen to ___ their goods by showing which items are being sold and how fast they are moving.
explanation: 词义辨析。keep track of：跟踪了解……的情况；keep pace with：跟上……的步伐；keep in touch with：和……保持联系；keep company with：与……结交，与……同行。根据句意可知，选 A。

stem: That field ___ a good crop of potatoes last year.
explanation: 词义辨析。plant：种植，主语通常是人；grow：生长，一般指作物自身的生长；raise：抬高，提起；yield：出产（作物），主语可以是土地等。根据句意可知，选 D。

stem: The destruction of these cultural relics was a loss that no amount of money could ___.
explanation: 词义辨析。stand up to：经得起，经得住；make up for：弥补……；come up with：想出；put up with：容忍。根据句意“损失是金钱弥补不了的”可知，选 B。

stem: When people do not ___ to acceptable standards of behavior, they are bound to offend other people.
explanation: 词义辨析。confirm：证实，确认；conform：遵从，遵守，符合，多与 to 搭配使用；confine：限制，禁闭；inform：通知，告知。根据句意可知，选 B。

stem: It was such a big challenge. Luckily, the student was just about to ___ the questions when he suddenly found the answer.
explanation: 词义辨析。arrive at：到达（某地）；work out：解出，找到（解决办法等）；work on：从事；give up：放弃。根据句意“这个学生正要放弃问题时突然找到了答案”可知，选 D。

stem: Once he starts talking about ancient China, ___.
options: there is no stopping of him
explanation: 固定用法。本题考查固定句型 There be no doing，意为“不可能……，没有什么能……”，stop 为及物动词，直接跟宾语，不需要加介词。故选 C。

stem: They decided to chase the cow away ___ it did more damage to the crops.
explanation: 词义辨析。unless：除非，如果不；before：在……之前；until：直到；although：尽管。根据句意“在牛对庄稼做出更大伤害之前把它赶走”可知，选 B。

stem: The ___ of blood always makes him feel sick.
explanation: 词义辨析。sight：看见，看到，强调视觉所接受的景象；look：看，强调运用视觉器官；view：视力，视野；glance：匆忙一瞥。根据句意可知，选 A。

stem: In Britain, the best time for sightseeing is ___ spring and early summer.
explanation: 词义辨析。later：较晚时候的，以后的；latter：后者；last：最近的；late：晚的，晚期的，late spring 意为“春末，晚春”。故选 D。

stem: I should like to rent a house which is modern, comfortable and ___, in a quiet neighborhood.
explanation: 词义辨析。in all：总共，总计；after all：毕竟；above all：最重要的是；over all：全面地。根据句意“最重要的是处于一片宁静之地”可知，选 C。

stem: When Mr. Jones gets old, he will ___ over his business to his son.
explanation: 词义辨析。take over：接管；think over：思考；hand over：把……移交给；get over：克服，度过。根据句意“把事业交给他的儿子”可知，选 C。

stem: I've already told you that I'm going to buy it, ___.
explanation: 状语从句。however 引导的让步状语从句语序为 however + adj./adv. + 主语 + 谓语，符合此结构的只有 A 项。D 项中 no matter how 也可引导让步状语从句，但其后缺少 much。故选 A。

stem: Free medical treatment in this country covers ___ illness of all kinds for all the citizens.
explanation: 词义辨析。normal：正常的；average：平均的；regular：有规律的，定期的；ordinary：普通的。根据句意“覆盖全体公民的所有普通疾病”可知，选 D。

stem:
【Passage 1 原文】
Tom arrived at the bus station quite early for Paris bus. The bus for Paris would not leave until five to twelve. He saw a lot of people waiting in the station. Some were standing in line, and others were walking around. There was a group of schoolgirls. Their teacher was trying to keep them in line. Tom looked around but there was no place for him to sit.
He walked into the station café（咖啡馆）. He looked up at the clock there. It was only twenty to twelve. He found a seat and sat down before a large mirror on the wall. Just then, Mike, one of Tom's workmates came in and sat with Tom.
“What time is your bus?” asked Mike.
“There's plenty of time yet,” answered Tom.
“Well, I'll get you some more tea then,” said Mike.
They talked while drinking. Then Tom looked at the clock again. “Op! It's going backward!” he cried. “A few minutes ago it was twenty to twelve and now it's half past eleven.” He was puzzled on that.
“You're looking at the clock in the mirror.” said Mike. Tom was so sorry for that. The next bus was not to leave for another hour. Since then Tom has never liked mirrors.

【题目】Tom went into the station cafe because ___.
options: Mike asked him to have a cup of tea
there were a group of schoolgirls there
it was quite early and he could find a seat there
he wanted to have a drink with his workmate there
explanation: 事实细节题。根据第一段第一句和最后一句可知，由于到达时时间尚早（quite early）且没有空位可坐（no place for him to sit），因此他走进了车站咖啡厅，因为他可以在那里找到位子。故选 C。

【题目】Which of the following is true?
options: Tom arrived in Paris on time.
The next bus left after half an hour.
After that Tom didn't like clocks any longer.
Tom looked at the clock in the mirror only once.
explanation: 事实细节题。汤姆已错过车，最后一班车再等一个小时也不会开，从那时起汤姆再也不喜欢镜子（而非钟表），故 A、B、C 错误。由全文可知汤姆的车 11:55 开，第一次看钟是 11:40，第二次看却变成 11:30，即他只看了一次镜子中的时间。故选 D。

stem:
【Passage 2 原文】
Baths have long been considered of medical importance to man. In Greece there are the ruins of a water system for baths built over 3,000 years ago. The Romans had warm public baths. In some baths, as many as 3,000 persons could bathe at the same time.
Treating disease by taking baths has been popular for centuries. Modern medical baths first became popular in Europe and by the late 1700s bathing had also become popular in the United States.
For many years frequent bathing was believed to be bad for one's health. Ordinary bathing just to keep clean was avoided, and perfume was often used to cover up body smells!
By the 1700s doctors began to say that soap and water were good for health. They believed that it was good for people to be clean. Slowly, people began to bathe more frequently. During the Victorian Age of the late 19th century, taking a bath on Saturday night became common.
In the United States ordinary bathing was slow to become popular. During the 18th and early 19th centuries. many Americans were known as “The Great Unwashed!” In one American city, for example, a person was only allowed to take a bath every thirty days! That was a law!
Frequency of bathing today is partly a matter of habit. People know that bathing for cleanliness is important to health. Doctors know that dirty bodies increase the chance of diseases. As a result, in the United States, people generally bathe often. Some people bathe once a day at least. They consider a daily bath necessary to good health.

【题目】A water system for baths was built by ___ over 3,000 years ago.
explanation: 事实细节题。根据第一段第二句“In Greece there are the ruins of a water system for baths built over 3000 years ago.”可知，三千多年前希腊人修建了洗浴供水系统。故选 B。

【Passage 4 原文】
On Thursday afternoon Mrs. Clarke, dressed for gong out, took her handbag with her money and her key in it, pulled the door behind her to lock it and went to the Over 60s Club. She always went there on Thursdays. It was a nice outing for an old woman who lived alone.
At six o'clock she came home, let herself on and at once smelt cigarette smoke. Cigarette smoke in her house? How? How? Had someone got in? She checked the back door and the windows. All were locked or fastened, as usual. There was no sign of forced entry.
Over a cup of tea she wondered whether someone might have a key that fitted her front door—“a master key” perhaps. So she stayed at home the following Thursday. Nothing happened. Was anyone watching her movements? On the Thursday after that she went out at her usual time, dressed as usual, but she didn't go to the club. Instead she took a short cut home again, letting herself in through her garden and the back door. She settled down to wait.
It was just after four o'clock when the front door bell rang. Mrs. Clarke was making a cup of tea at the time. The bell rang again, and then she heard her letter-box being pushed open. With the kettle of boiling water in her hand, she moved quietly towards the front door. A long piece of wire appeared through the letter-box, and then a hand. The wire turned and caught around the knob(门把)on the door-lock. Mrs. Clarke raised the kettle and poured the water over the hand. There was a shout outside, and the skin seemed to drop off the fingers like a glove. The wire fell to the floor, the hand was pulled back, and Mrs. Clarke heard the sound of running feet.

【题目】Mrs. Clarke looked forward to Thursday because she ___.
options: joined in a special activity in the club
had a special visitor to meet
explanation: 事实细节题。根据文章第一段可知，克拉克夫人每周四都要去“the Over 60s Club”，而且这对她来说也是不错的出行，所以她很期待周四。故选 C。

stem: The committee ___ a conclusion only after days of discussion.
explanation: 考查词语搭配。draw/reach/arrive at/come to a conclusion 为固定搭配，意为“得出结论”。故选 A。

stem: The next afternoon I went to ___ Miss Barkley again, but found her out.
explanation: 考查词义辨析。call for：要求、需要；call on(sb.)：拜访（某人）；call up：给……打电话、使回忆起；call off：取消。根据句意可知选 B。

stem: He said ___ was not within his power to answer the question.
explanation: 考查 it 的用法。it 在从句中作形式主语，指代后面真正的主语 to answer the question。故选 D。

stem: ___ to hurt her, he did not tell her the truth.
explanation: 考查非谓语动词作状语。逻辑主语 he 与 want 为逻辑上的主谓关系，且句中没有明显的时间先后标志，应用现在分词作原因状语；分词的否定式在分词前直接加 not。not to want 表目的和将来，不合题意；C、D 语法结构不正确。故选 B。

stem: He risked ___ his house when his company went bankrupt.
explanation: 考查非谓语动词。risk doing sth. 意为“冒险做某事”，risk 后不能跟动词不定式，排除 A、D；B 项为现在分词完成式，表示动作发生在 risked 之前，不合题意。故选 C。

stem: I didn't heat ___ because there was too much noise where I was sitting.
explanation: 考查宾语从句。由连接代词或连接副词引导的宾语从句应用陈述语序，排除 A、C 两项；D 项表将来，不合题意。故选 B。

stem: I can't ___ this type of computer, it's too expensive.
explanation: 考查词义辨析。cost：花费；spend：花费（时间/金钱）；afford：买得起、负担得起；pay：支付。根据句意可知选 C。

stem: Faced with the crisis, the girl looked pale, but was quite ___.
explanation: 考查词义辨析。silent：沉默的、寂静的；quiet：宁静的、安静的；still：静止的、无风的；calm：镇定的、沉着的。根据句意可知选 D。

stem: He didn't allow ___ in his room. Actually he did not allow his family ___ at all.
explanation: 考查非谓语动词。allow doing sth. 意为“允许做某事”；allow sb. to do sth. 意为“允许某人做某事”。故选 B。

stem: George took ___ of the fine weather to do a day's work in his garden.
explanation: 考查词语搭配。take advantage of：利用、占……的便宜；take charge of：负责、掌管；B、C 无此搭配。根据句意可知选 A。

stem: I was very tired. Otherwise, I ___ to the theatre with you.
explanation: 考查虚拟语气。由句意和 Otherwise（否则、不然）可知，此处表示与过去事实相反的假设，谓语动词应用“would have + 过去分词”的形式。故选 D。

stem: Seldom ___ in such a rude way.
explanation: 考查倒装句和动词语态。否定副词 never、hardly、seldom 等位于句首时，句子应用倒装结构，即将助动词、情态动词或 be 动词提到主语之前，排除 A、B；同时 we 与 treat 为逻辑上的动宾关系，应用被动语态。故选 C。

stem: This well-known international organization was ___ several years ago.
explanation: 考查词义辨析。set up：建立、设立；make up：组成、化妆；take up：开始从事、占用；get up：起床、站起来。根据句意可知选 A。

stem: The policeman ___ the thief down the road.
explanation: 考查词义辨析。chase：追捕、追赶；run：跑、移动；rush：急速行进；race：（和……）竞赛。根据句意可知选 A。

stem: Every means ___ but it's not so effective.
explanation: 考查主谓一致和动词语态。“every + 单数可数名词”作主语时，谓语动词用单数，排除 A、C；means 与 try 为逻辑上的动宾关系，应用被动语态。故选 B。

stem: By the time class was over, the rain ___ .
explanation: 考查动词时态。by the time 意为“到……时候（为止）”，引导时间状语从句；若从句为一般过去时，主句应用过去完成时，表示截止到从句动作发生时主句动作已完成。故选 C。

stem: Fortunately, the demonstration ___ to be quite peaceful.
explanation: 考查词义辨析。turn in：归还、上交；turn out：结果是、证明是；turn off：关掉；turn up：出现、开大。根据句意可知选 B。

stem: Mr. Johnson, together with his wife and two daughters, ___ to arrive this evening.
explanation: 考查主谓一致和动词时态。由 as well as、along with、together with 等连接并列主语时，意义上更强调前面的主语，谓语动词应与 Mr. Johnson 的人称和数保持一致，用单数；由时间状语 this evening 可知应用 be to do 结构表将来。故选 D。

stem: ___ , he'll make a first-class tennis player.
explanation: 考查非谓语动词。be 与 give 之间为逻辑上的动宾关系，应用过去分词；非谓语动词短语 Given time 作条件状语，相当于条件状语从句 If he is given time。故选 A。

stem: We shall have an opportunity to exchange ___ tomorrow.
explanation: 考查词义辨析。sight：视力、景象；opinion：意见，exchange opinions 意为“交流意见”；thought：思想、想法；mind：心思、思维。根据句意可知选 B。

stem: Many birds ___ the island during the summer months.
explanation: 考查词义辨析。settle 意为“定居、把……放好”，作及物动词时后面应接被安置的对象，此处若选 settle 应用被动语态且 the island 前缺介词，排除 A；join：连接、参加；move：移动；visit：访问、逗留。根据句意可知选 D。

stem: Thank you for the ___ you did me to move the sofa upstairs.
explanation: 考查词语搭配。do sb. a favor 为固定搭配，意为“帮某人一个忙”。空处与 to 之间为省略引导词 that/which 的定语从句，修饰 the favor。故选 A。

stem: I paid him 50 dollars for the painting, but its real ___ must be about 500 dollars.
explanation: 考查词义辨析。fee：服务费、费用；value：（商品）价值；price：价格、价钱；fare：车费、票价。根据句意可知选 B。

stem: We enjoyed ourselves very much at the party. You ___ with us.
explanation: 考查情态动词。should have + 过去分词表示过去本应该做而实际上没有做的行为，符合题意；must have + 过去分词表示对过去情况的肯定推测；must + 动词原形表示对现在情况的肯定推测；should + 动词原形表示现在或将来应该做某事。故选 C。

stem: Where is the ___ writing desk?
explanation: 考查形容词（限定词）词序。多个形容词作定语修饰同一名词时排列顺序固定：限定描绘大长高，形状年龄和新老；颜色国籍出材料，作用类别往后靠。round 为形状应紧挨中心词；small 为尺寸大小应放在 round 前；charming 为描绘性词汇应放在最前面。故选 C。

stem: It would be unwise to ___ too much importance to these opinion polls.
explanation: 考查词语搭配。attach too much importance to 意为“太过重视……，太在意……”，为固定搭配。故选 D。

stem: We haven't been able to find out the ___ of the rumor.
explanation: 考查词义辨析。source：来源、出处；cause：原因、理由；resource：资源、资料；reason：理由、原因。根据句意选 A。

stem: I ___ to come to your house last night but it rained hard.
explanation: 考查词义辨析。think：考虑，其后一般接名词或从句；attend：出席、参加；intend：想要、打算，intend to do sth. 意为“打算做某事”；consider：认为。根据句意及空后的不定式可知选 C。

stem: The cost of the reconstruction would ___ from 2.5 to 3 million pounds.
explanation: 考查词语搭配。deserve：应受、应得；spend：花费、消耗，常用 spend time/money on sth.；range：（在一定范围内）变化，range from A to B 意为“在从 A 到 B 的范围内变化”；include：包含。故选 C。

stem: The authorities have refused to ___ him a visa to visit England.
explanation: 考查词义辨析。arrange：安排、整理；agree：同意；approve：赞成、批准；grant：给予、准许，grant sb. sth. 意为“授予某人某物”。根据句意可知选 D。

stem: By the time I saw the job advertised, it was too late to ___ .
explanation: 考查词义辨析。ask：询问、要求；request：请求、要求；demand：要求、需求；apply：申请、应用。根据句意（申请工作已经太晚）可知选 D。

stem: Unfortunately he didn't ___ to read the agreement carefully before signing it.
explanation: 考查词义辨析。bother：费心、麻烦，bother to do sth. 意为“费心做某事”；disturb 与 interrupt 后面一般不接不定式；trouble：使忧虑。根据句意可知选 A。

stem: Import for the first three months this year is larger than for the ___ period last year.
explanation: 考查词义辨析。relating：相关的；concerning：关于、涉及；regarding：关于、就……而论；corresponding：相应的、一致的，corresponding period 意为“同期”。根据句意可知选 C。

stem: I bought a new bicycle, ___ was very high.
explanation: 考查定语从句。空处引导非限制性定语从句，price 与 bicycle 之间为所属关系，应用 the price of which，which 指代先行词 bicycle，且因 of which 的修饰 price 前必须加定冠词 the。故选 A。

stem: The furniture arrived ___ , so we had to send it back.
explanation: 考查非谓语动词。furniture 与 damage 为逻辑上的动宾关系，damage 应用过去分词形式，表示被动和完成。故选 D。

Many parents complain that their teenage children are rebelling (叛逆). I wish it were so. At this age you ought to be growing away from your parents. You should be learning to stand on your own feet.

Many parents complain that their teenage children are rebelling (叛逆). I wish it were so. At this age you ought to be growing away from your parents. You should be learning to stand on your own feet.
But take a good look at the present rebellion. It seems that teenagers are all taking the same way of showing that disagree with their parents. They say they want to dress as they please, but all of them wear the same clothes. They set off in new directions in music, but all of them end up listening to the same record. Their reason for thinking or acting is that the others are doing it that way.
It has become harder and harder for a teenager to stand up against the popularity wave and go his or her own way. These days every teenager can learn from the advertisements what a teenager should have and be. And many of today's parents have come to award (给予) high marks for the popularity of their children. All this adds up to a great barrier for the teenager who wants to find his or her own path.
But the barrier is worth climbing over. The path is worth following. You may want to listen to classical music instead of going to a party. You may want to collect rocks when everyone else is collecting records and stamps. Well, go to it. Find yourself. Be yourself. Popularity will come with the people who respect you for who you are. That's the only kind of popularity that really counts.

【题目】In this passage the writer wants to tell ___ .
options: teenagers how to decide things for themselves
readers how to be popular with other people
parents how to control and guide their children
people how to understand and respect each other
explanation: 主旨大意题。文中“stand on your own feet”“go his or her own way”“find his or her own path”“Find yourself. Be yourself.”表明作者想告诉青少年要找到自我、做自己、学会独立。A 项“告诉青少年为自己作决定”符合题意。故选 A。

【Passage 3 原文】
A moment's drilling by the dentist may make us nervous and upset. Many of us cannot stand pain. To avoid the pain of a drilling that may last perhaps a minute or two, we demand the needle that deadens the nerves around the tooth.
Now it's true that the human body has developed its millions of nerves to be highly aware of what goes on both inside and outside it. This helps us adjust to the world. Without our nerves and our brain, we wouldn't know what's happening. But we pay for our sensitivity. We can feel pain when the slightest thing is wring with any part of our body. The history of torture (酷刑) is based on the human body being open to pain.
But there is a way to handle pain. Some Indian monks can sit on a bed of nails. Fakirs (托钵增) can put a needle right through an arm, and feel no pain. This ability that some humans have developed to handle pain should give us ideas about how the mind can deal with pain.
The big thing in standing pain is our attitude toward it. If the dentist says this will hurt a little, it helps us to accept the pain. By staying relaxed, and by treating the pain as an interesting sensation (感觉), we can handle the pain calmly. After all, although pain is an unpleasant sensation, it is still a sensation, and sensations are the stuff of life.

【题目】The word "deaden" in paragraph 1 probably means "___ ".
explanation: 词语理解题。根据第一段可知，我们要求注射药物来麻痹牙齿周围的神经，可推知 deaden 与 restrain（抑制）意义相近。increase：增加；improve：改善；excite：刺激。故选 B。

【Passage 4 原文】
There is a popular belief among parents that schools are no longer interested in spelling. No school I have taught in has ever ignored spelling or considered it unimportant as a basic skill. There are, however, vastly different ideas about how to teach it, or how much priority (优先) it must be given over general language development and writing ability. The problem is how to encourage a child to express himself freely and confidently in writing without holding him back with the complexities (复杂性) of spelling.
If spelling becomes the only focus of his teacher's in interest, clearly a bright child will be likely to play safe. He will tend to write only words within his spelling range, choosing to avoid adventurous language. That's why teachers often encourage the early use of dictionaries and pay attention to content rather than technical ability.
I was once shocked to read on the bottom of a piece of writing about a personal experience: "This work is terrible! There are far too many spelling errors in the writing, but it was also a sad reflection on the teacher who had feelings." The teacher was not wrong to draw attention to the errors, but of his priorities had centered on the child's ideas, an expression of his disappointment with the presentation would have encouraged the pupil to improve his writing.

【题目】Which of the following is true according to paragraph 1?
options: Parents are not interested in spelling.
Schools are not interested in spelling.
Teachers must give top priority to spelling.
explanation: 推理判断题。根据第一段最后一句可知，问题是如何在不受拼写复杂单词阻碍的情况下鼓励孩子自由、自信地写作，可推知单词拼写复杂会阻碍自由写作。故选 D。

Most people agree that the direct, assertive (过分自信的) American personality is a virtue, but it sometimes surprises foreigners. In many cultures, respect for older people or those in positions of authority keeps others from expressing their true feelings. But in the U.S., children often argue with their parents, students may disagree with their teachers, and citizens may express opposition to the actions of the government. If the soup has anything in it or the meat is too tough to eat, the diner can complain to the waiter; if the boss makes a mistake, an employee will politely point it out.

Some straight talk about the American character must include the admission that Americans have their faults. The extremely competitive nature of Americans is probably their worst fault. Of course, competition isn’t always bad. As a matter of fact, it promotes excellence by encouraging individuals and businesses to try to do their best. But the desire to get ahead of others sometimes causes people to do things that are unkind and even dishonest. Also, Americans admire what is practical, fast, efficient, and fresh. Sometimes they fail to understand and appreciate practices that have greater respect for more traditional, leisurely ways of doing things. On the other hand, people from other cultures ma dislike the practical, challenging American lifestyle.

Despite culture differences, most foreigners give Americans credit for their virtues. Americans are generally viewed as friendly, adaptable, energetic, and kind-hearted. Most newcomers to the U.S. like Americans, and the felling is usually mutual. Perhaps the greatest American virtue is a deep interest in new ideas and new people. In a nation of immigrants, the foreigner does not remain an outsider for long.

【Passage 4 原文】
We arc all interested in equality, but while some people try to protect the school examination system in the name of equality, others, still in the name of equality, want only to destroy it.

Any society which is interested in equality of opportunity and standards of achievement must regularly test its pupils. The standards may be changed – no examination is perfect-but to have no tests or examinations would mean the end of equality and of standards. There are groups of people who oppose this view and who do not believe either in examinations or in any controls in school or on teachers. This would mean everything would depend on luck since every pupil would depend on the values and the purpose of each teacher.

Without examinations, employers will look for employees from the highly respected schools and from families known to them –a form of favoritism will replace equality. At the moment, the bright child from an ill-respected school can show certificates to prove he is suitable for a job, while the lack of a certificate indicates the unsuitability of a dull child attending a well-respected school. This defense of excellence and opportunity would disappear if examinations were taken away, and the bright child from a poor family would be a prisoner of his school’s reputation, unable to compete for employment with the child from the favored school.

The opponents of the examination system suggest that examinations are an evil force because they show differences between pupils. According to these people, there must be no special, different academic class. They have even suggested that there should be no form of difference in sport or any other area: all jobs or posts should be filled by unsystematic selection. The selection would be made by people who themselves are probably selected by some computer.

explanation: [词语理解题] 根据第一段“…but while some people try to protect the school examination system in name of equality, others…want only to destroy it.”可知，it 指代的是学校考试制度（school examination system）。故选D。

Any society which is interested in equality of opportunity and standards of achievement must regularly test its pupils. The standards may be changed – no examination is perfect-but to have no tests or examinations would mean the end of equality and of standards. There are groups of people who oppose this view and who do not believe either in examinations or in any controls in school or on teachers. This would mean everything would depend on luck since every pupil would depend on the values and the purpose of each teacher.

Without examinations, employers will look for employees from the highly respected schools and from families known to them –a form of favoritism will replace equality. At the moment, the bright child from an ill-respected school can show certificates to prove he is suitable for a job, while the lack of a certificate indicates the unsuitability of a dull child attending a well-respected school. This defense of excellence and opportunity would disappear if examinations were taken away, and the bright child from a poor family would be a prisoner of his school’s reputation, unable to compete for employment with the child from the favored school.

The opponents of the examination system suggest that examinations are an evil force because they show differences between pupils. According to these people, there must be no special, different academic class. They have even suggested that there should be no form of difference in sport or any other area: all jobs or posts should be filled by unsystematic selection. The selection would be made by people who themselves are probably selected by some computer.

【题目】The word “favoritism” in paragraph 3 is used to describe the phenomenon that ___.
options: bright children usually get better jobs
poor children with certificates are favored in job markets
children attending ordinary schools achieve great success
children from well-respected schools will have good jobs
explanation: [事实细节题] 根据第三段第一句“Without examinations, employers will look for employees from the highly respected schools…favoritism will replace equality.”可知，如果没有考试，偏袒会取代平等，名校的学生会有更好的就业机会。故选D。

stem:
——Where are you going, Tom?
——To Bill's workshop. The engine of my car needs ___.
explanation: 非谓语动词。当need/want/require作“需要”讲，且前面主语是指物的名词或代词时，其后常用动名词的主动形式或不定式的被动形式作宾语表示被动意义，意为“某物需要……”，故空处应用repairing或to be repaired。故选A。

stem: The luggage is ___ heavy to carry all the way home. Let's call a taxi.
explanation: 固定用法。too...to...意为“太……而不能……”，为固定结构，其他三项均没有这种用法。故选B。

stem: Our teacher suggested that each of us ___ a study plan for the long summer vacation.
explanation: 虚拟语气。suggest作“建议”讲时，其后的宾语从句应用虚拟语气，即谓语动词用“should+动词原形”的形式，should可以省略。故选A。

stem: If you had told me earlier, I ___ to meet you at the hotel.
explanation: 虚拟语气。根据从句的谓语动词had told可知本句是对过去情况的虚拟，主句的谓语动词应用“would/could/might have+过去分词”的形式。故选D。

stem: Kin went to visit the teacher in the primary school ___ he worked three years ago.
explanation: 定语从句。空处为定语从句的引导词，先行词是表示地点的the primary school，且从句缺少地点状语，所以应用关系副词where引导。故选B。

stem: The language school started a new ___ to help young learners with reading and writing.
explanation: 词义辨析。program:程序、计划、课程；design:设计、图案；event:事件、（比赛）项目；progress:进步、发展。根据句意可知，选A。

stem: Always keep in mind that more fruit, vegetables and ___ exercises will keep us healthy.
explanation: 词义辨析。regular:定期的、有规律的；normal:正常的、正规的；average:平均的、一般的；ordinary:普通的、平常的。根据句意可知，选A。

stem: Peter often accompanies his parents to the concert, ___ he does not like pop music at all.
explanation: 词义辨析。根据句意可知前后表示让步关系。as和though均有“尽管，虽然”之意，但as引导的让步状语从句一般要用倒装结构，而though引导的让步状语从句可以不倒装，符合题意；if引导条件状语从句，since引导时间和原因状语从句。故选D。

stem: Mr Brown would like to make ___ on his house, but he was disappointed.
explanation: 词语搭配。make a profit on:在……上赚钱、从……中获利，为固定搭配。故选C。

stem: It is Allen's first time to speak to the public, but I am sure he will get ___ his nervousness.
explanation: 词义辨析。get away:离开、逃脱；get off:动身、脱下；get over:克服、恢复；get through:通过、到达、完成、耗尽。根据句意可知，选C。

stem: If you are not satisfied with this pair, I will get you ___ one of the same size and colour.
explanation: 词义辨析。another one:又一个，指相同种类中的另一个，相当于one more；other只能和复数名词连用；more:更多的；less:较少的。根据句意可知，选B。

stem: It is reported that a plane has ___ in the mountainous area near the borderline of that country.
explanation: 词义辨析。crash:坠毁、撞碎；crush:压碎、使变皱；flash:使闪光；clash:冲突、争论。根据句意可知，选A。

stem:
——Where is my cell phone? I can't find it.
——Well, you ___ have put it somewhere.
explanation: 情态动词。must have done表示对过去发生事情的肯定推测，符合题意；should/ought to have done表示本应该做某事而实际没做；would have done表示对过去发生事情的假设。故选B。

stem: I think we should stop arguing and work together, if we want to get ___ neat a solution to the problem.
explanation: 词语搭配。get somewhere意为“取得进展”，为固定搭配。故选D。

stem: The gardener ___ the boy not to step on the grass.
explanation: 词义辨析。suggest:建议，常用于suggest sth./doing sth.结构；charge:控告、收（费）；warn:告诫、警告，常用于warn sb. (not) to do sth.结构；insist:坚持，后面常接宾语从句。根据句意可知，选C。

stem:
——I'm afraid we must go now if we don't want to get caught in the traffic jam.
——OK. ___.
explanation: 情景交际。It doesn't matter:没关系；You're welcome:不客气、不用谢；Take care:小心、当心；Never mind:没关系、别提了。根据语境可知，选C。

stem: You might not like the way Sam behaves, but please be kind to him. ___, he is your grandfather.
explanation: 词义辨析。after all:毕竟、终究；above all:首先、最重要的是；in all:总共、总计；at all一般与not连用，构成not at all表示“一点也不”。根据句意可知，选A。

stem: We mention the importance of giving up smoking once and again, but hardly ___ it.
explanation: 倒装句和动词时态。表示否定意义的词或词组位于句首时，句子要用倒装，根据hardly一词可首先排除C、D两项；根据句意此处应用现在完成时，表示之前的动作对现在造成的影响。故选B。

stem: Tom's room is in a terrible mess, everything seems ___ in it.
explanation: 词义辨析。out of control:失控；out of date:过时；out of order:不整洁、杂乱无序；out of service:失效、停止运行。根据句意此处指“房间里乱七八糟”，所以选C。

stem: At the 60th anniversary, the guests sitting in the front are those ___ graduates from the university.
explanation: 词义辨析。faithful:忠实的、忠诚的；distinguished:杰出的、卓越的，常用来修饰人；impressive:给人印象深刻的；interesting:有趣的。根据句意此处指“那些优秀毕业生”，所以选B。

stem: We were caught in a traffic jam. By the time we arrived at the airport the plane ___.
explanation: 动词时态。by the time意为“到……的时候（为止）”，可引导时间状语从句；如果从句中的谓语动词为过去式，主句应用过去完成时。take off所表示的动作发生在arrived所表示的动作之前，即动作发生在“过去的过去”，所以主句应用过去完成时。故选D。

stem: ___ is not known yet.
options: Although he is serious about it
No matter how we will do the task
Whether we will go outing or not
Unless they come to see us
explanation: 主语从句。分析句子结构可知本句缺少主语，四个选项中只有C项可以充当主语从句。Although和no matter how常引导让步状语从句，unless常引导条件状语从句，均不符合题意。故选C。

stem: You can't rely on Jane as she is ___ changing her mind and you will never know what she is going to do next.
explanation: 词义辨析。occasionally:偶尔、间或；rarely:罕见地、很少；scarcely:几乎不、绝不；constantly:不断地、经常地。根据句意可知，选D。

stem: Kids will soon get tired of learning ___ more than they can.
options: if they are expected to learn
if they are learned to expect
explanation: 动词时态和语态。空后为if引导的条件状语从句，主句是一般将来时，从句要用一般现在时表示将来，且they与expect之间为逻辑上的动宾关系，所以要用被动语态。故选B。

stem: Many people prefer the bowls made of steel to the ___ made of plastic.
explanation: 词义辨析（代词用法）。空处指代前面的the bowls，用于指代前面提到过的可数名词复数时，为避免重复可用the ones来替代。故选C。

stem: ___ from far away, the 600-meter tower is stretching into the sky.
explanation: 非谓语动词。本题考查非谓语动词短语作状语，the 600-meter tower与see是逻辑上的动宾关系，所以要用过去分词seen表示被动意义。故选D。

stem: The tribe had been living in that part of the area for generations until the civil war ___.
explanation: 词义辨析。break down:毁掉、出故障；break off:中断、突然停止；break out:突发、爆发；break up:破碎、分裂。根据句意可知，选C。

stem: The young man had decided to give up the chance of studying abroad, ___ surprised his parents a lot.
explanation: 定语从句。空处引导非限制性定语从句，从句成分不完整，缺少主语。空处所填关系词用来指代前面整个句子，且在从句中作主语，所以只能用which。故选C。

stem: ___ , Martin can reach the branch of that tall tree at the gate.
explanation: 状语从句和倒装句。as意为“尽管”，引导让步状语从句时应用倒装语序，即将表语、状语等提至as前面，用来表示强调。本题应将作表语的short提至句首，所以选D。

stem: The temperature is likely to go down next week. ___, we will have to cancel the outdoor activities.
explanation: 词义辨析。in that case:如果那样的话、既然是那样，符合题意；in case作“免得，以防”讲时引导目的状语从句，作“假使”讲时引导条件状语从句；in no case:绝不，若置于句首句子要用倒装；in any case:在任何情况下。根据句意可知，选A。

【Passage 1 原文】
On Thursday afternoon Mrs. Clarke, dressed for going out, look her handbag with her money and her key in it, locked the door and went to the club. She always went there on Thursdays. It was a nice outing for an old woman who lived alone.

At six o’ clock she came home, let herself in and at once smelt cigarette smoke. Cigarette smoke in her house? How ? Haw? Had someone got in? She checked the back door and the windows. All were locked or fastened, as usual. There was no sign of forced entry.

Over a cup of tea she wondered whether someone had a key that fitted her front door----“a master key” perhaps. So she stayed at home the following Thursday. Nothing happened. Was anyone watching her movements? On the Thursday after that she went out at her usual time, dressed as usual, but she didn’t go to the club. Instead she took a short cut home again, letting herself in through her garden and the back door. She settled down to wait.

It was just after four o’ clock when the front door bell rang. Mrs. Clarke was making a cup of tea at the time. The bell rang again, and then she heard her letter-box being pushed open. With the kettle of boiling water in her hand, she moved quietly towards the front door. A long piece of wire appeared through the letter box, and then a hand. The wire turned and caught around the knob in the door-lock. Mrs. Clarke raised the kettle and poured the water over the hand. There was a shout outside, and the skin seemed to drop off the fingers like a glove. The wire fell to the floor,and the hand was pulled back, Mrs. Clarke heard the sound of running feet.

【题目】On Thursday, Mrs Clarke usually ___.
explanation: 事实细节题。根据第一段第一、二句“On Thursday afternoon Mrs. Clarke…went to the club. She always went there on Thursdays.”可知，Clarke夫人经常会在周四去俱乐部。故选B。

【Passage 2 原文】
We find that bright children are rarely held back by mixed-ability teaching. On the contrary, both their knowledge and experience are enriched. We feel that there are many disadvantages in dividing pupils into different groups. It does not take into account the fact that children develop at different rates. It can have a bad effect on both the bright and the not-so-bright child. After all, it can be quite discouraging to be at the bottom of the top grade!

Besides, it is rather unreal to grade people just according to their intellectual ability. This is only one aspect of their total personality. We are concerned to develop the abilities of all our pupils to the full, not just their academic ability. We also value personal qualities and social skills, and we find that mixed-ability teaching contributes to all these aspects of learning.

In our classrooms, we work in various ways. The pupils often work in groups; this gives them the opportunity to learn to co-operate, to share, and to develop leadership skills. They also learn how to cope with personal problems as well as how to think, to make decisions, to analyze and evaluate, and to communicate effectively. The pupils learn from each other as well as from the teacher.

Sometimes the pupils work in pairs’ sometimes they work on individual tasks and assignments, and they can do this at their own speed. They also have some formal class teaching when this is appropriate. We encourage our pupils to use the library, and we teach them the skills they need in order to do this effectively. An advanced pupil can do advanced work; it does not matter how old the child is. We expect our pupils to do their best, not their least, and we give them every encouragement to attain this goal.

【题目】The phrase “held back” in Line 1 means being ___.
explanation: 词语理解题。根据第一段第一、二句可知，混班教学并不会阻止聪明孩子们的发展，反而会丰富他们的知识和经验，所以held back是“被阻止发展”的意思，与选项B表达的意思相同。故选B。

【Passage 3 原文】
In the 1960s, medical researchers Thomas Holmes and Richard Rahe developed a checklist of stressful events. They appreciated the tricky point that any major change can be stressful. Negative events like “serious illness of a family member” were high on the list, but so were some positive life-changing events, like marriage. When you take the Holmes-Rahe test you must remember that the score does not reflect how you deal with stress---it only shows how much you have to deal with. And we now know that the way you handle these events dramatically affects your chances of staying healthy.

By the early 1970s, hundreds of similar studies had followed Holmes and Rahe. And millions of Americans who work and live under stress worried over the reports. Somehow, the research was described briefly in a memorable message. Women’ s magazines ran headlines like “Stress causes illness!” If you want to stay physically and mentally healthy, the articles said, avoid stressful events.

But such simple advice is impossible to follow. Even if stressful events are dangerous, many---like the death of a loved one----are impossible to avoid. Moreover, any warning to avoid all stressful events is a prescription（处方）for staying away from opportunities as well as trouble. Since any change can be stressful, a person who wanted to be completely free of stress would never marry, have a child,and take a new job or move.

The notion that all stress makes you sick also ignores a lot of what we know about people. It assumes we’ re all weak and passive in the face of difficulties. But what about human initiative and creativity? Many people who come through periods of stress with more physical and mental energy than they had before. We also know that a long time without change or challenge can lead to boredom, and physical and metal strain.

【题目】Holmes-Rahe made a medical research on ___.
options: what to do to avoid stress
what to do to cope with stress
what kind of events can cause stress
what kind of stress can cause changes
explanation: 事实细节题。根据第一段第一句可知，Holmes和Rahe就“什么事情会产生压力”进行了一项医学研究。故选C。

【Passage 4 原文】
Even plants can run a fever, especially when they’re under attack by insects or disease. But unlike humans, plants can have their temperature taken from 3,000 feet away----straight up. A decade ago, adapting the infrared（红外线）scanning technology developed for military purposes and other satellites, physicist Stephen Paley came up with a quick way to take the temperature of crops to determine which ones are under attack. The goal was to let farmers precisely target pesticide（杀虫剂）spraying rather than rain poison on a whole field, which always includes plants that don’t have pest（害虫）problems.

Even better, Paley’s Remote Scanning Services Company could detect crop problems before they became visible to the eye. An infrared scanner, on a plane flying at 3,000 feet at night, measured the heat send out by crops. The data was turned into a color-coded map showing where plants were running “fevers”. Farmers could then spot-spray, using 50 to 70 percent less pesticide than they otherwise would.

The bad news is that Paley’s company closed down in 1984, after only three years. Farmers resisted the new technology and long-term supporters were hard to find. But with the renewed concern about pesticides on produce, and refinements in infrared scanning, Paley hopes to get back into operation. Agriculture experts have no doubt about how the technology works. “This technique can be used on 75 percent of agricultural land in the United States”, says George Oerther of Texas A＆M. Ray Jackson, who recently retired from the Department of Agriculture, thinks long-distance infrared crop scanning could be adopted by the end of the decade, but only if Paley finds the financial support which he failed to obtain 10 years ago.

【题目】Plant will run a fever when they are ___.
explanation: 事实细节题。根据第一段第一句可知，当植物被害虫攻击或者生病的时候，植物会发烧。故选C。

stem: I was in ___ that I forgot to lock the door when I left.
explanation: 考查 so/such...that... 的区别。so 是副词，修饰形容词或副词；such 是形容词，修饰名词。hurry 是名词，应用 such 修饰并加不定冠词 a，故选 B。

stem: I am worried about my brother. I am not sure ___ he has arrived at the school or not.
explanation: 考查宾语从句。sure 后为宾语从句，从句不缺任何成分；whether 与后面的 or not 构成固定搭配，意为“是否”，故选 A。

stem: She is old enough ___ on her own.
explanation: 考查非谓语动词。“形容词+enough+不定式”为固定结构，意为“足够……可以做某事”，故选 B。

stem: He was very excited to read the news ___ Mo Yan had won the Nobel Prize for literature.
explanation: 考查同位语从句。空处引导同位语从句解释抽象名词 news，从句不缺成分，只起连接作用，应用 that，故选 D。

stem: I do not have my own room, ___.
explanation: 考查倒装句。前句否定情况也适用于后句，用 neither/nor 引导倒装；由 do not 可知助动词应用 does，故选 A。

stem: I think you should buy this novel. It is really worth ___.
explanation: 考查非谓语动词。be worth doing 为固定搭配，动名词用主动形式表被动意义，故选 A。

stem: Though the firefighters tried very hard to ___ the fire, it still caused at least five people’ s death.
explanation: 考查词义辨析。put off 推迟；put out 扑灭；put on 穿上；put forward 提出。根据句意“灭火”选 B。

stem: He could hardly tell the differences between the twins because they look ___ each other.
explanation: 考查词义辨析。look like 后可接宾语，意为“看上去像”；look alike 后不接宾语。句中有宾语 each other，故选 D。

stem: By the time you come back, I ___ cleaning the house.
explanation: 考查动词时态。By the time you come back 表示将来某时间前已完成某事，主句应用将来完成时，故选 B。

stem: Chinese people spend ___ money on travelling today as they did ten years ago.
explanation: 考查倍数表达法。用“倍数+as+原级+as”结构，不可数名词 money 用 much 修饰，故选 C。

stem: She wants to study abroad so she has to ___ some money every month to prepare for that.
explanation: 考查词义辨析。set aside 省出、留出（钱或时间）；set up 建立；set about 着手做；set out 动身。故选 A。

stem: John had planned to leave but be decided to stay in the hotel for ___ two days because of the heavy rain.

stem: Parents should cooperate with teacher and ___ themselves in their children’ s education.

stem: The teacher is very ___ to the needs of her students and she can adapt her teaching very flexibly.

stem: You can borrow my book, ___ you promise to give it back to me by the end of this month.

stem: ___ from Buckingham Palace, this trip takes you to the best of London’ s sights.

stem: Applicants for the Olympic volunteers must be able to ___ excellent services to meet the demands of the Games.

stem: It is the natural scenery ___ earns the city a good reputation.

stem: Many young couples do not take marriage ___ and they get married and divorced easily.

stem: Mary is not happy to live with her parents. What she wants ___ more privacy while what her parents expect ___ more tome to be with her.

stem: She is one of the top students in her class ___ she studies very hard.

stem: The brown bear escaped from the zoo, which was a ___ to everyone in the town.

【Passage 1 原文】
This past fall semester, at Duke University, there were two students who were taking Organic Chemistry. They did pretty well on all of the tests and the midterms and labs, etc. , such that going into the final they had a solid “A”. These two friends were so confident going into the final that the weekend before finals’ week, even though the Chemistry final was on Monday, they decided to go up to the University of Virginia and have a party with some friends up there. So they did this and had a great time. However, with the aftereffects of alcohol and everything, they overslept all day Sunday and didn’ t make it back to Duke until early Monday morning. Rather than taking the final then, what they did was to find Professor Aldric after the final and explain to him why they missed the final. They told him that they went up to UVA for the weekend, and had planned to come back in tome to study, but they had a flat tire (爆胎) on the way back and didn’ t have a spare and couldn’ t get help for a long time and so were late getting back to campus. Aldric thought this over and then agreed that they could make up the final on the following day. The two guys were overjoyed and relieved. So, they studied that night and went in the next day at the time that Aldric had told them. He placed them in separate rooms and handed each of them a test booklet and told them to begin. They looked at the first problem, which was something simple about free radical formation and was worth 5 points. “Cool,” they thought, “this is going to be easy.” They did that problem and then turned the page. They were unprepared, however, for what they saw on the next page. It said: (95 points) Which tire was flat?

they were invited by their friends
they were not worried about the exam at all
they forgot the arrangement of the final exam
explanation: 事实细节题。第一段“These two friends were so confident going into the final that…”说明两位学生对考试非常自信，才决定周末去参加派对，选项 C“他们一点也不担心考试”符合题意。故选 C。

【Passage 2 原文】
A large, detached（独立的）house not only ensures privacy. It is also a status symbol. The “magnificent home” is set in a big garden. Of course, this kind of house is an unrealistic dream for most people. But even a small detached house, surrounded by a garden, gives the required suggestion of rural life which is dear to the hearts of many British people. Most people would be happy to live in a cottage（村舍）, and if this is a thatched（茅草的）cottage, suggestive of a pre-industrial age, so much the better. Most people try to avoid living in a block of flats (what the Americans call “apartment blocks”). Flats, they feel, provide the least amount of privacy. With a few exceptions, mostly in certain locations in central London, flats are the cheapest kind of home. The people who live in them are those who cannot afford to live anywhere else. The dislike of living in flats is very strong. In the 1950s millions of poorer people lived in old, cold, uncomfortable nineteenth century houses, often with only an outside toilet and no bathroom. During the next twenty years many of them were given new “high rise” blocks of flats to live in which, with central heating and bathrooms, were much more comfortable and were surrounded by grassy open spaces. But people hated their new homes. They said they felt cut off from the world with all those floors up. They missed the neighborliness. They couldn’ t keep a watchful eye on their children playing down there in those lovely green spaces. The new high-rise blocks quickly got broken. The lifts didn’ t work. The corridors were dark. Windows were damaged and were not repaired. There was graffiti all over the walls.

【题目】British people prefer ___.
explanation: 推理判断题。第一段最后一句“Most people would be happy to live in a cottage…”以及第二段首句“Most people try to avoid living in a block of flats…”可推知英国人喜欢村舍而不适合公寓，故选 B。

【Passage 3 原文】
When we are not engaged in thinking about some definite problem, we usually spend about 95 percent of our time thinking about ourselves. Now, if we stop thinking about ourselves for a while and begin to think of other persons’ good points, things will be quite different. One of the most neglected virtues is appreciation. Somehow, we neglect to praise our son or daughter when he or she brings home a good report card, and we fail to encourage our children when they first succeed in baking a cake or building a birdhouse. Nothing pleases children more than this kind of parental interest and approval. The next time you enjoy delicious food at restaurant, send word to the cook that it is excellently prepared, and when a tired salesperson shows you unusual politeness, please mention it. Every minister, lecturer and public speaker knows the discouragement of pouring himself or herself out to an audience and not receiving any appreciative comment. What applies to professionals applies doubly to workers in offices, shops and factories and our families and friends. In our interpersonal relations we should never forget that all our associates are human beings and hunger for appreciation. It is the legal tender that all souls enjoy. Try to be friendly and appreciate in your daily life, and you will be surprised how that will change your life and the world.

【题目】According to the passage, people ___.
options: spend a lot of time thinking about others
think about themselves most of the time
spend little time thinking about themselves
think more about others than themselves
explanation: 事实细节题。第一段“…we usually spend about 95 percent of our time thinking about ourselves.”可知人们大部分时间想自己的事，故选 B。

stem: 假设你是李明，最近参加了某旅行社（travel agency）组织的一次旅游，但你对此旅行很不满意。请你向客服(customer service)写一封投诉信，阐述投诉的原因（如：酒店、饮食、交通、及费用等）并提出你期待的解决办法。
answer: Dear Customer Service, My name is Li Ming and I am a customer of your travel agency. I’m writing to express my dissatisfaction with the service of your travel agency during my recent travel. First of all, during the trip the tour guide took us to many different places to go shopping, which cost us too much money and time. In addition, most of us thought that the guide was not competent enough because he knew little about the scenic spots. What was worse, the food that was served to us was of poor quality and the accommodation conditions were rather awful. At last, the provided transportation was not convenient at all, which wasted us a lot of time.
explanation: 考查投诉信写作。需以李明身份向旅行社客服写一封投诉信，阐述对旅行（导游、饮食、住宿、交通、费用等）的不满并提出期待的解决办法，属应用文写作。

stem: Hearing that he had passed ___ health examination, he immediately made ___ call to his parents.

stem: ___ you are, friends are an important part of life at every stage.

stem: Although we waited more than half an hour, Mary didn't turn ___ at the conference room.
explanation: 考点：词义辨析。turn up 意为“到场，露面，出现”，与“玛丽没有出现在会议室”相符。故选 C。

stem: Maria hadn't seen me for a few years, but she ___ my voice on the phone immediately.
explanation: 考点：词义辨析。recognize 意为“认出，识别”，与“立刻从电话里听出我的声音”相符。故选 B。

stem: The student needed a letter of ___ to apply for the post of a secretary.
explanation: 考点：词义辨析。a letter of recommendation 为固定搭配，意为“推荐信”。故选 B。

stem: He is well-prepared for the presentation about the new project and feels ___ that the head of department will like his idea.
explanation: 考点：词义辨析。confident 意为“确信的，有信心的”，与“有信心部门领导会喜欢他的想法”相符。故选 D。

stem: Tom's mother was shocked that Tom had got head ___ in a car accident.

stem: It was very late when we decided to travel on May Day holiday, but luckily we ___ to find a hotel at a reasonable price.

stem: The famous writer, ___ writings for China Daily I appreciate a lot, is invited to give a speech in our university.
explanation: 考点：定语从句。空处引导非限制性定语从句并在从句中作 writings（作品）的定语，应用 whose 引导。故选 B。

stem: If people ___ overanxious about remembering something, they will forget it.

stem: We were very angry ___ Peter as he spoiled our picnic.

stem: The teenager is ___ to be a member of the basketball team.
explanation: 考点：固定用法。“sb./sth.+be+adj.+enough to do”为固定句型，enough 修饰形容词时须后置。故选 B。

stem: Finally, I have ___ interesting to share with you, and I am sure you will be interested in it.
explanation: 考点：词义辨析。something 意为“某件事”，用于肯定句，符合句意。故选 B。

stem: Since we have ___ money left, we can't afford the expensive computer.
explanation: 考点：词义辨析。money 为不可数名词，排除 a few/few；little 意为“很少”，表否定意义，与“买不起那台昂贵的电脑”相符。故选 C。

stem: If you want to join our club, you ___ follow our rules.
explanation: 考点：情态动词。must 意为“必须”，强调说话人主观上认为有必要，符合“必须遵守规则”。故选 D。

stem: When Max rushed to the classroom, his classmates ___ exercises attentively.
explanation: 考点：动词时态。when 引导的时间状语从句为一般过去时，主句表示从句动作发生时动作正在进行，应用过去进行时。故选 C。

stem: The little girl recovered her strength when the drug ___.
explanation: 考点：词义辨析。take effect 意为“（药等）见效，起作用”，符合句意。故选 B。

stem: Patrick bought her two handbags as gifts, but ___ of them was her style.
explanation: 考点：词义辨析。由 two 可排除 none/all；but 表转折，neither 意为“两者都不”。故选 C。

stem: ___ his surprise, he got an offer of postgraduate study from Beijing University.
explanation: 考点：词语搭配。to one's surprise 为固定搭配，意为“让某人惊讶的是”。故选 B。

stem: The boss required us to ___ a recent photo to the application form via emails.
explanation: 考点：词义辨析。attach sth. to sth. 意为“把某物附在另一物上”，符合“在申请表上附照片”。故选 A。

stem: Bill Gates is often thought to be the richest man in the world. ___, his personal life seems not luxury.
explanation: 考点：词义辨析。前后两句为转折关系，however 意为“然而，可是”。故选 C。

stem: Mr. Lin ___ to New York before, so the host family went to the airport to pick him up.
explanation: 考点：动词时态。由 before 可知动作发生在 went 所表示的动作之前，即“过去的过去”，应用过去完成时。故选 D。

stem: Though the ___ drama is wonderful, I guess most audiences will be tired as it is too long.
explanation: 考点：数词的用法。“基数词+名词”用连字符构成形容词时名词须用单数，four-hour 相当于 four hours'，意为“四个小时的”。故选 A。

stem: You'd better get the task ___ as soon as possible, otherwise you might not complete it on time.
explanation: 考点：非谓语动词。get sth. done 意为“使某事被做”，符合“尽快完成任务”。故选 C。

stem: Since we lacked enough time and support, we didn't know ___ to solve the problem.
explanation: 考点：词义辨析。how to solve the problem 为“疑问词+to do”结构，意为“如何解决这个问题”。故选 D。

stem: ___ the opportunity to interview the famous star made her overjoyed.
explanation: 考点：非谓语动词。逻辑主语“她”与 provide 之间为动宾关系，应用动名词的被动式 being provided 作主语。故选 A。

stem: We missed the last train to London, or we ___ more museums the day before yesterday.
explanation: 考点：虚拟语气。or 引出含蓄虚拟条件，对过去情况的假设应用“would have+过去分词”。故选 B。

stem: Your parents don't believe what you said about your future, ___?
explanation: 考点：反意疑问句。陈述句部分主句 Your parents don't believe 为否定，反意疑问部分应用肯定形式；主句为一般现在时，故用 do they。故选 B。

stem: The daughter begged her father to give up smoking ___ his own health.
explanation: 考点：词义辨析。for the sake of 意为“为了……起见，因为……的缘故”，符合“为了他自己的健康”。故选 D。

stem: The more the salesman explained, ___.
explanation: 考点：比较等级。本题考查“the+比较级…, the+比较级…”句型，表示“越……就越……”，bored 的比较级为 more bored。故选 C。

【Passage 2 原文】
A punctual person is in the habit of doing a thing at the proper time and is never late in keeping an appointment.
The unpunctual man, on the contrary, never does what he has to do at the proper time. He is always in a hurry and in the end loses both time and his good name. A lost thing may be found again, but the lost time can never be regained. Time is more valuable than material things. In fact, time is life itself. The unpunctual man is forever wasting and mismanaging his most valuable asset(财产) as well as other's. The unpunctual person is always complaining that he finds no time to answer letters, return calls or keep appointments promptly. But the man who really has a great deal to do is very careful of his time and seldom complains of want of it. He knows that he can get through his huge amount of work unless he faithfully keeps every piece of work when it has to be attended to.
Failure to be punctual in keeping one's appointments is the sign of disrespect towards others. If a person is invited to dinner and arrives later than the appointed time, he keeps all the other guests waiting for him. Usually this will be regarded as a great disrespect to the host and all other guests present.
Unpunctuality, moreover, is very harmful when it comes to do one's duty, whether public or private. Imagine how it would be if those who are put in charge of important tasks failed to be at their proper place at the appointed time. A man who is known to be habitually unpunctual is never trusted by his friends or fellow men.

【题目】The main difference between a punctual person and an unpunctual person is that a punctual person ___.
options: has lots of appointments while an unpunctual one has few appointments
does everything at the right time while an unpunctual one seldom does so
has much time to do everything while an unpunctual one has little time to do anything
does everything ahead of time while an unpunctual one does everything behind schedule
explanation: 事实细节题。第一段及第二段第一句指出，守时的人习惯按时做事，而不守时的人很少按时完成必须做的事。故选 B。

For the past 20 years, they had been on good terms farming side by side, sharing machinery, and trading labor and goods as needed. Jack had to go into town, so he helped the carpenter get the materials ready and then he was off for the day. The carpenter worked hard all that day measuring, sawing and nailing. About sunset when Jack returned, the carpenter had just finished his job.
Jack's eyes opened wide, his jaw dropped. There was no fence there at all. It was a bridge—a bridge stretching from one side of the stream to the other! A fine piece of work! His younger brother was coming toward them with hands outstretched. “You are quite a fellow to build this bridge after all I've said and done.” The two brothers stood at each end of the bridge, and then they met in the middle, taking each other's hand.
They turned to see the carpenter lift his toolbox onto his shoulder. “No, wait! Stay a few days. I have a lot of other projects for you,” said Jack. “I'd love to stay on,” the carpenter said, “but I have many more bridges to build.”

【Passage 4 原文】
Batteries can power anything from small sensors to large systems. While scientists are finding ways to make them smaller but even more powerful, problems can arise when these batteries are much larger and heavier than the devices themselves. The researchers at University of Missouri (MU) are developing a nuclear energy source that is smaller, lighter and more efficient.
“To provide enough power, we need certain methods with high energy density (密度),” said Jae Kwon, assistant professor of electrical and computer engineering at MU, “The radioisotope (放射性同位素) battery can provide power density that is much higher than chemical batteries.”
Kwon and his research team have been working on building a small nuclear battery, presently the size and thickness of a penny, intended to power various systems. Although nuclear batteries can cause concerns, Kwon said they are safe.
“People hear the word ‘nuclear' and think of something very dangerous,” he said, “However, nuclear power sources have already been safely powering a variety of devices, such as pace-makers, space satellites and underwater systems.”
His new idea is not only in the battery's size, but also in its semiconductor. Kwon's battery uses a liquid semiconductor rather than a solid semiconductor.
“The key part of using a radioactive battery is that when you harvest the energy, part of the radiation energy can damage the lattice structure (晶体结构) of the solid semiconductor,” Kwon said, “By using a liquid semiconductor, we believe we can minimize that problem.”
Together with J. David Robertson, chemistry professor and associate director of the MU Research Reactor, Kwon is working to build and test the battery. In the future, they hope to increase the battery's power, shrink its size and try with various other materials. Kwon said that battery could be thinner than the thickness of human hair.

explanation: 事实细节题。第一段开头即介绍电池的用途，故文章是以 introduction（介绍）开篇的。故选 A。

He was just 12 years old when he died. But he brought courage and hope to people around the world.

Although Nakosi Johnson died, he is still remembered today as an AIDS fighter. This young boy challenged his government's AIDS policies and millions of South Africans in the fight against the disease.

Johnson was the longest survivor born HIV positive （艾滋病病毒携带者）. He survived with this deadly disease for 12 years before it claimed his life.

At first, Johnson was expected to live for nine months when his foster mother, Gail Johnson took him in at the age of two. She now runs Nkosi's Haven across the town from his house in Melville. The Haven is home to 20 children living with HIV or AIDS and 11 of their mothers.

Johnson attracted the world's attention and stole the hearts of thousands of people across the world at the 13th International AIDS Conference in Durban in July, 2000. He stood in front of a large audience including South African President Thabo Mbeki. He told them that he wanted AZT, a drug used to treat AIDS patients, to be given to HIV-postive pregnant (怀孕的) women to prevent the disease from being passed on to their unborn babies. He received a loud cheer at the end of his speech. Johnson's speech was broadcast live across the world. With views beyond his age and even a sense of humor, Johnson soon became an international sign of the fight against AIDS and HIV.

he had his own idea to fight against the disease

【Passage 2 原文】
What should you think about in trying to find your career? You are probably better at some school subjects than others. These may show strengths that you can use in your work. A boy who is good at mathematics can use that in an engineering career. A girl who spells well and likes English may be good at office work. So it is important to do well at school. On the other hand, you may not have any specially strong or weak subjects but your records show a general satisfactory standard. Although not all the subjects can be used directly in a job, they may have indirect value. Knowledge of history is not required for most jobs but if history is one of your good subjects you will have learned to remember the facts and details. That is the ability that can be useful in many jobs.

Your school may have taught you skills, such as typing or technical drawing, which you can use in your work. You may be good at mental work or cookery and look for a job where you can improve these skills.

If you have had a part-time job on Saturdays or in the summer, think what you gained from it. If nothing else, you may have learned how to get to work on time, to follow the instruction and to get on with older workers. You may learn to give correct change in a shop, for example. Just as important, you may become interested in a particular industry or career you see from the inside in a part-time job.

Facing your weak points is also part of knowing yourself. Perhaps you are a poor speller or cannot add up a column of figures. It is better to face any weaknesses than to pretend they do not exist. Your school record, for instance, may not be good, yet it is an important part of your background. You should not be apologetic about it but instead recognize that you will have a chance of a fresh start at work.

【题目】What does the first paragraph mainly tell us?
options: The importance of finding a good job.
The importance of one's ability in school.
The importance of doing well in school work.
The importance of being good at all the subjects.
explanation: 主旨题。第一段强调在学校学好功课很重要（it is important to do well at school），故选 C。

【Passage 3 原文】
Until the twentieth century, women did not often participate in sports. Part of the explanation for this is that women simply did not have time. Many women cooked, cleaned, and took care of children. They were so busy that they did not have time for sports. A second reason, especially in the late nineteenth century, is that a woman's image at that time was one of weakness, illness, and delicacy. In the Victorian era, people thought that it was unladylike for a woman to be involved in any sports activity.

There have been changes in both the view of women in the modern world, and also changes within the world of sports. These changes have allowed many more women to participate in sports. The general view of women has changed substantially since the Victorian era. Women are no longer considered delicate. People do not think it is unladylike for a woman to compete in sports. Women who win in sports activities are highly regarded. Many women now take part in sports and games of many different kinds, and enjoy doing so. This development is partly the result of a change in the image of women in the modern world.

Women are also more active in sports now because of two changes in sports. First, in the early twentieth century, women began to compete regularly in the Olympics. Also, the number of events for women in the Olympics has been growing quite steadily. The fact that women can compete in the Olympics encourages many to become active in the various Olympic activities. In more recent years, television has had a noticeable effect on the popularity of women's professional sports. Many women's tennis matches and golf matches are on TV, along with many other competitions. Seeing women in professional sports on TV has made certain sports much more popular among women, as amateurs and as professionals.

explanation: 细节题。第一段指出过去女性忙于做饭、打扫、照顾孩子，没有时间运动，故选 A。

New research is trying to find how we learn and make decisions exactly. To the brain, a new thought or idea is like a spider. If it works hard enough, a web of knowledge spins out from it. Photos of the brain taken during learning actually show a kind of nerve cells firing, growing, and forming new connections. This is fascinating in itself, but what's even more fascinating is that failure can cause this to happen.

That's right; failure can enhance your brain.

Stanford University psychologist Carol Dweck has compared the brain waves of people with growth and fixed mind-sets. She finds that, when those with growth mind-sets fail at a task, they would enter a more focused mental state. And as they try again and again, they improve. In effect, they've learned, and their brains have“grown.”Those with fixed mind-sets, however, never enter this focused state of learning and show little advancement.

Antoine Bechara, a professor of psychology and neuroscience at the University of Southern California, has taken Dweck's work a step further. He recently isolated two equally sized centers in the brain. These areas interact during the decision-making process. Although more research is needed, these centers may turn out to be the physical locations for Dweck's twin mind-sets.

“We always knew people could learn from their mistakes, but now we're finding out exactly how and where this happens,” explains Bechara. “In a normally functioning brain, failure is taken as an opportunity for learning and strengthening the species.”

【题目】According to the passage, like a spider, a new thought or idea could ___.
explanation: 细节题。第一段指出新想法像蜘蛛一样，若足够努力就会织出知识的网（a web of knowledge），故选 D。

【完形填空原文】
At the beginning of 1993, Harrison Textile Company, a plant that makes clothes for people, suffered a disaster. The plant, equipment, stock and so on, were ___51___ down and turned to ashes. More than 3,000 employees were completely ___52___ in the face of the unexpected disaster. Sad and depressed, they returned home, waiting with despair ___53___ the chairman to declare the bankruptcy（破产）and unemployment. But ___54___, after long waiting, the company posted each person ___55___ a letter: the company would pay one month's salary to all employees of the company.

When all of the workers almost ___56___ all hope for the life of future, the company's letter ___57___ again: the company would pay one month's salary to all the staff of the company.

If the ___58___ letter surprised and delighted thousands of employees, the second letter almost ___59___ them to tears. Indeed, the whole country was suffering a lot in such a bad situation that many ___60___ had no way for living, so who would not be touched by such ___61___?

Just as the chairman ___62___, on the day of receiving the second letter, thousands of employees rushed back to ___63___. They cleaned up the ruins, tidied up the situations after the ___64___ and worked again, and some of them even took the initiative to contact the interrupted supply of goods.

Three months ___65___, Harrison Company came to life. Today Harrison Company has become the largest American textile company.

【第51空】请选择最合适的选项。
explanation: 词义辨析。工厂被烧毁、化为灰烬，burn down 意为“烧毁”，故选 A。

stem: He told me that he ___ here for ten minutes.

stem: In today's class, he appeared to be ___ than he used to be.

stem: As the clock ___ twelve tonight, the deadline will have passed.

stem: ___ receiving the book, she went over the most interesting chapters first.

stem: In the corner of the library, I found a book ___ cover was stained with ink.
explanation: 考查定语从句。空处修饰先行词 a book，在从句中作定语，应用关系代词 whose。故选 B。

stem: Our campus is ___ big that we need a bike to make it.
explanation: 考查状语从句。so...that... 表示“如此……以至于……”，so 为副词，后接形容词；such 为限定词，后接名词。此处修饰形容词 big。故选 B。

stem: Judy hardly joins in any class activities, ___?

stem: The students ___ outdoors when the visitors arrived.

stem: I might fail, but I will keep doing it ___.

stem: Every detail should be considered ___ that it won't happen again.

stem: Please give me one more day, and I will get ___ ready.

stem: She ___ to work from 9 a.m. to 9 p.m., six days a week.

stem: Online shopping, when properly ___, can save a lot of time, money and energy.

stem: The country will double its ___ to reduce the economic losses caused by the earthquake.

stem: ___ high cost of living in big cities, many graduates choose to work in small cities.

stem: Busy preparing a report, he couldn't ___ the noise, and had to keep all the windows shut.

stem: It is an online platform ___ people can buy and sell many kinds of things.

stem: I like a house with a beautiful garden, but I don't have enough money to buy ___.
explanation: 考查代词。one 泛指前面提到的同类事物中的一个（同类不同物）；it 特指前面提到的同一事物。此处指“买一座那样的房子”，为同类泛指，故选 A。

stem: A survey has ___ that a growing number of people are overweight.
explanation: 考查词义辨析。reflect 反映、映出；release 释放、发布；remark 评论、说起；reveal 揭示、显示、透露。此处指调查“显示”。故选 D。

stem: He lifted the huge rock ___ drop it on his own feet.
explanation: 考查词义辨析。so as to 以便；but to 无此搭配；only to 不料、竟然（表出乎意料的结果）；in order to 为了。此处表示意外结果“不料砸到自己脚上”。故选 C。

stem: As the economy develops, the living standards of the people have improved ___.
explanation: 考查词义辨析。urgently 紧急地；significantly 有重大意义地、显著地；properly 恰当地；frequently 频繁地。此处指“显著提高”。故选 B。

stem: It was on his 22nd birthday ___ the young man received his first job offer.
explanation: 考查强调句。此处为 It is/was + 被强调部分 + that/who… 的强调句型，被强调部分是时间状语，只能用 that。故选 C。

stem: She visited several museums to ___ information for her research project.
explanation: 考查词义辨析。receive 收到；pick 挑选、摘；acquire（通过努力）获得、习得；gather 集合、搜集（信息）。此处指“为研究项目搜集信息”。故选 D。

stem:

— ___.
explanation: 考查情景交际。Go ahead 开始吧、先走；Help yourself 请自便；It's up to you 由你决定；No problem 没问题。此处表示“由你决定”。故选 C。

Each year, 1.3 million people worldwide die in car accidents. Ninety-four percent of those crashes are due to human error. This is a tragedy that self-driving vehicles can help prevent. That's because computers can think better and react earlier than people.

Self-driving cars will also help speed up the shift toward increased ride sharing and reduced car ownership. Many people already use ride-sharing services instead of owning their own cars. Fewer cars also means less pollution and fewer parking spaces. That would make room for more parks, bike lanes, and businesses.

Real-world testing is critical to getting this technology ready for nationwide use. That's why some companies are testing self-driving cars in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, and Tempe, Arizona. Both cities have welcomed this technology with open arms.

A better future is within reach. We already have the technology. While it won't happen overnight, self-driving cars will be an important part of the future of transportation.

【Passage 2 原文】
Jack London, one of America's major writers of adventure tales, was born in California in 1876. During his life, London worked at many jobs. His broad life experiences would become the background for his writing.

London loved to read. As a teenager, he spent many hours educating himself at the public library. He attended college at the University of California at Berkeley, but he stayed for only six months. He thought Berkeley was "not lively enough" and wanted to do something more exciting.

London wrote stories about working people and the hard times they had making a living. He knew their problems firsthand. He worked as a sailor, factory employee, and railroad worker, to name just a few of his many jobs.

Like many people of the time, London caught the Gold Rush Fever. In 1897, he headed for Alaska. He didn't find gold, but he discovered something even more valuable. He discovered that people enjoyed listening to the stories he made up with his vivid imagination. London entertained the miners with story after story. Later, using his experiences during the Gold Rush, he created many more colorful stories.

London resolved to live a full, exciting life. He once said that he would rather be a shooting star than a sleepy and permanent planet. Each day, he pushed himself. Once London determined that he was going to be a writer, nothing could stop him. His goal was to write at least one thousand words every day. He refused to stop even when he was sick. In eighteen years, the writer published fifty-one books and hundreds of articles. He was the best-selling and highest-paid author of his day. Many people also considered him to be the best writer.

【题目】What inspired Jack London's adventure tales?
explanation: 推理判断题。第一段最后一句 “His broad life experiences would become the background for his writing” 可知其广泛的人生经历成为写作背景。故选 A。

Like many people of the time, London caught the Gold Rush Fever. In 1897, he headed for Alaska. He didn't find gold, but he discovered something even more valuable. He discovered that people enjoyed listening to the stories he made up with his vivid imagination. London entertained the miners with story after story. Later, using his experiences during the Gold Rush, he created many more colorful stories.

London resolved to live a full, exciting life. He once said that he would rather be a shooting star than a sleepy and permanent planet. Each day, he pushed himself. Once London determined that he was going to be a writer, nothing could stop him. His goal was to write at least one thousand words every day. He refused to stop even when he was sick. In eighteen years, the writer published fifty-one books and hundreds of articles. He was the best-selling and highest-paid author of his day. Many people also considered him to be the best writer.

【Passage 3 原文】
Does stress, anger, or sadness drive you to eat? Do you turn to food for comfort, or when you're bored? Many people do. If you often eat for emotional reasons instead of because you're physically hungry, that can be a problem.

Obeying the urge to eat more than you need is certain to gain weight. It's an even bigger problem if you already have health conditions like high blood pressure.

You can get back in control of your emotional eating. The surprising part is, it's not really about food at all. The solution to emotional eating is less about eating than it is about emotions. You can start with a simple step. "Make a list of what is stressing you, and make a plan to take control of the situation," New York psychologist Patricia Farrell says. If you can change the situation, go for it. If the problem is out of your control, you can manage the way you think about it. If you can notice your stress in the moment, you can choose how you respond, rather than reacting the way you have in the past. It helps to add a delay between the urge to eat and the actual eating. That gives you time to check in with how you're feeling and why you want to eat.

When you get the urge to eat a cookie out of sadness or boredom, remember that you have the choice to wait it out. "Tell yourself to have it later," Farrell says. Even if it doesn't successfully delaying the snack helps you feel more in control.

In addition, consider talking with a doctor so you can better understand what's going on with you and the best way to handle it.

【题目】Emotional eating happens when a person is ___.
explanation: 推理判断题。第一段说压力、愤怒或悲伤会驱使进食，为寻求安慰或因无聊而吃，均属负面情绪。故选 C。
